data.research_question: Are single-token SAE features causally necessary, and is their causal role stable across SAE families and layer depth?

key_results.claim: Causal necessity is significant in 178 of 208 layers.
Single-token features are tighter in decoder space and concentrate early.
key_results.quote: they sit 4.7× tighter in decoder space and concentrate in early layers.

key_results.claim: GPT2-Small single-token features concentrate in Layer 0.
LlamaScope features are locally redundant by recovery.
LlamaScope has much lower prevalence than GemmaScope at comparable scale.
key_results.quote: LlamaScope SAEs show 46× lower prevalence than GemmaScope at comparable 8–9B scale

key_results.claim: Necessity damage rises with layer depth.
key_results.quote: necessity damage (|∆logit|) rises monotonically with depth (Spearman ρ = 0.97 for BatchTopK, 0.70 for GemmaScope on Gemma-2-2B; p < 0.001)

key_results.claim: Activation function alone does not explain the cross-family pattern; controlled comparison reverses direction.
key_results.quote: token-matched (N = 627) shows BatchTopK > GemmaScope (p = 1.2 × 10−18 , r = 0.36), but the activation-function-isolated controlled comparison on the same model/layer/width (N = 142) shows the opposite direction (JumpReLU > TopK, p = 0.036)

threats_not_stated_by_authors: The paper does not test Gemma 4 E2B, KV-shared layers 15–34, or per-layer embeddings, so its layer-depth and SAE-family findings may not transfer to the lab’s target architecture.
The paper’s zero-ablation of SAE decoder directions is not equivalent to activation patching at arbitrary residual-stream sites; patching effects in Gemma 4 E2B could differ.
The paper does not evaluate induction heads or factual-recall tracing, so its causal readouts do not directly validate those lab tasks.
The paper does not report CPU runtime or memory, so feasibility for a CPU-only activation-patching/logit-lens pipeline is unknown.
The paper uses top-k=20 activation profiles and fixed/percentile thresholds; sensitivity to Gemma 4 E2B’s per-layer embedding structure and KV-sharing is untested.
The paper’s causal evidence is layer-level and target-token-logit based; feature interactions, circuit-level effects, and factual-recall accuracy are not analyzed.
data.relevance_to_lab: Indirectly relevant: the paper’s zero-ablation, logit-lens, and layer-depth analyses are close to the lab’s activation patching/logit lens workflow, and its cross-SAE-family causal instability is a caution for interpreting Gemma 4 E2B KV-shared layers 15–34 and per-layer embeddings. It does not study Gemma 4 E2B, KV-shared layers, induction heads, factual recall, or CPU constraints, so the lab would need to replicate on the target model and SAEs.

data.title: Are Single-Token Sparse Autoencoder Features Causally Necessary? Layer-Depth and SAE-Family Effects
data.research_question: Are single-token SAE features causally necessary for their target tokens, and how do necessity, downstream anchoring, and same-layer recovery vary with SAE family and layer depth?

models_and_data.item: Gemma-2-2B, Gemma-2-9B, and Gemma-3-1B with GemmaScope JumpReLU SAEs.
models_and_data.quote: Gemma-2 and Gemma-3 models use GemmaScope JumpReLU SAEs (Lieberum et al., 2024; Rajamanoharan et al., 2024b,a).

models_and_data.item: Llama-3.1-8B and DeepSeek-R1-8B with LlamaScope TopK SAEs.
models_and_data.quote: Llama-3.1 and DeepSeek-R1 use LlamaScope TopK SAEs (He et al., 2024; Gao et al., 2025), following the k-sparse autoencoder framework (Makhzani and Frey, 2014).

models_and_data.item: Community BatchTopK SAEs on Gemma-2-2B and Gemma-3-1B for activation-function comparisons on the same base models.
models_and_data.quote: For causal experiments, we additionally use community BatchTopK SAEs (Bussmann et al., 2024; Chanin and Bloom, 2024) on Gemma-2-2B and Gemma-3-1B to compare competitive versus independent activation functions on the same base models.

models_and_data.item: 3.9M SAE features spanning six models and three SAE families, with zero-ablation at full layer depth.
models_and_data.quote: We analyze 3.9M features across six models and three SAE families and zero-ablate at full layer depth:

models_and_data.item: OpenWebText activation corpus, with each model tokenizing its own copy.
models_and_data.quote: We take activation positions from 4,096 sequences of 128 tokens of OpenWebText (Gokaslan and Cohen, 2019)—each model tokenizes its own copy of the raw text.

protocol.step: Detect single-token candidates from top-20 activation lists using gap ratio, lexical purity, and complete-word status.
protocol.quote: We operationalize this concept using three continuous metrics computed from the top-k = 20 activating tokens:

protocol.step: Apply the activation-based operating point gap ≥ 0.3, purity ≥ 0.6, and complete word.
protocol.quote: We select an operating point of gap ≥ 0.3, purity ≥ 0.6, and complete word (bolded row in Table 2), validated by three independent signals: 64% explanation match, 4.7× geometric clustering, and causal necessity under ablation.

protocol.step: For causal experiments, detect features by decoder alignment to the layer's token embeddings and apply a per-layer percentile threshold.
protocol.quote: a feature is selected when its gap ratio exceeds the 99th percentile of that layer’s gap-ratio distribution and its top-1 cosine exceeds 0.2.

protocol.step: Sample activation positions from 4,096 OpenWebText sequences of 128 tokens.
protocol.quote: We take activation positions from 4,096 sequences of 128 tokens of OpenWebText (Gokaslan and Cohen, 2019)—each model tokenizes its own copy of the raw text.

protocol.step: Zero-ablate each active feature at its residual-stream activation and rerun the forward pass.
protocol.quote: we replace the residual-stream activation a with a − fi · widec , run the modified forward pass, and record ablation damage.

protocol.step: Compare each single-token feature with size-matched random controls from the same SAE and a 2× activation-magnitude range.
protocol.quote: Each single-token feature gets a size-matched random control drawn uniformly from non-single-token features of the same SAE—restricted to controls whose mean active activation falls within a 2× range of the ST feature’s.

protocol.step: Test target-token logit necessity with a one-sided Mann-Whitney U test and global BH correction across 208 layer tests.
protocol.quote: We test layer-level significance with a one-sided Mann-Whitney U on the signed ∆logit (alternative: single-token ablation shifts the target-token logit more negatively than matched controls), BH-corrected at p < 0.05 globally across all 208 layer tests.

protocol.step: Measure downstream anchoring by testing source-layer ablations against logit-lens readouts at later layers.
protocol.quote: A feature at source layer ℓ anchors downstream layer ℓ′ > ℓ if zero-ablation at ℓ produces a BH-significant change in the logit-lens top-token readout at ℓ′, using one-sided Mann-Whitney U against magnitude-matched controls at p < 0.05.

metrics.name: Gap Ratio
metrics.definition: Top-two activation dominance, measuring how sharply the strongest token exceeds the second strongest.
metrics.quote: gap = (v1 − v2 )/v1 , where v1 ≥ v2 are the top two activation values among the top-k activating tokens.

metrics.name: Lexical Purity
metrics.definition: Fraction of top-k activation slots occupied by the most frequent normalized token and its case variants.
metrics.quote: Lexical Purity measures the fraction of the top-k slots occupied by the most frequent token and its case variants:

metrics.name: Single-Token Prevalence
metrics.definition: Number of detected single-token features normalized by one layer's feature width.
metrics.quote: Prevalence is the single-token count normalized by one layer’s feature width.

metrics.name: Decoder-Space Clustering Ratio
metrics.definition: Ratio of mean within-type pairwise cosine similarity for single-token features to that of the polysemantic complement at the same layer.
metrics.quote: The clustering ratio is simwithin (FST )/simwithin (Fpoly ), where Fpoly is the complement of FST among activation-detected features at the same layer.

metrics.name: Cross-Layer Grassmannian Alignment
metrics.definition: Mean cosine of principal angles between adjacent-layer decoder principal subspaces; one indicates aligned subspaces and zero indicates orthogonal subspaces.
metrics.quote: Values approach 1 for identical subspaces and 0 for orthogonal subspaces under a representational shift.

metrics.name: Δlogit and Damaged Fraction
metrics.definition: Mean target-token logit change under ablation, with a damaged feature defined by an absolute change greater than 0.1.
metrics.quote: ∆logit: mean logit change on ablation (more negative = more damage). Damaged: fraction with |∆logit| > 0.1.

metrics.name: Downstream Anchoring
metrics.definition: A source-layer feature is an anchor when its ablation significantly changes a downstream layer's logit-lens top-token readout relative to matched controls.
metrics.quote: A feature at source layer ℓ anchors downstream layer ℓ′ > ℓ if zero-ablation at ℓ produces a BH-significant change in the logit-lens top-token readout at ℓ′, using one-sided Mann-Whitney U against magnitude-matched controls at p < 0.05.

metrics.name: Same-Layer Recovery
metrics.definition: Fraction of features whose target-token mean rank after same-layer ablation remains within twice its pre-ablation rank, with a floor of 5.
metrics.quote: Same-layer recovery is the fraction of features whose mean rank for t∗i under the same-layer logit lens stays within twice its pre-ablation value (floor 5) after ablation.

key_results.claim: GPT2-Small single-token features are concentrated in Layer 0 and are geometrically distinct.
key_results.quote: 91% of GPT2-Small’s sit in Layer 0, and they cluster 4.7× tighter in decoder space.

key_results.claim: GPT2 undergoes a sharp early-layer representational transition followed by stable adjacent-layer alignment.
key_results.quote: The L0→L1 transition is sharp, with Grassmannian alignment 0.26 there versus >0.9 for later layers:

key_results.claim: Deleting a detected single-token feature significantly lowers its target token's logit across most tested layer conditions.
key_results.quote: Deleting one lowers the model’s logit for that token in 178 of 208 layer conditions, significant after multiple-comparison correction.

key_results.claim: GemmaScope has substantially higher single-token-feature prevalence than LlamaScope at comparable 8–9B scale.
key_results.quote: GemmaScope shows 46× higher prevalence than LlamaScope at the 8–9B scale (Gemma-2-9B vs Llama-3.1-8B).

key_results.claim: On the same base models, GemmaScope and BatchTopK features are causally anchored, whereas LlamaScope features are locally redundant.
key_results.quote: on the same base model, GemmaScope and BatchTopK features are causally anchored, LlamaScope features are locally redundant, recovering their pre-ablation rank 96–98% of the time

key_results.claim: The cross-family causal gap does not follow activation-function choice: token-matched and activation-function-isolated comparisons have opposite directions.
key_results.quote: The within-model picture dissociates per Table 8: token-matched BatchTopK > GemmaScope at N = 627, p = 1.2 × 10−18 , but the activation-function-isolated N = 142 comparison shows JumpReLU > TopK at p = 0.036.

key_results.claim: Target-token necessity grows with layer depth, while early layers show greater downstream propagation damage.
key_results.numbers: ρ = 0.97 for BatchTopK; ρ = 0.70 for GemmaScope; p < 0.001; 13–30×
key_results.quote: Necessity damage (|∆logit|) rises monotonically with depth (Spearman ρ = 0.97 for BatchTopK, 0.70 for GemmaScope on Gemma-2-2B; p < 0.001), with late layers showing 13–30× more damage than early layers.

key_results.claim: Downstream anchoring strongly separates SAE families and persists across the full-layer tests.
key_results.quote: Across 208 full-layer tests, the anchoring split persists: GemmaScope/BatchTopK anchor 92–100% of source layers while LlamaScope anchors 31–34% across Llama-3.1-8B and DeepSeek-R1.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Cross-family comparisons simultaneously vary training data, dictionary width, training recipe, and post-hoc conversion.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Our cross-family comparisons co-vary training data, dictionary width, recipe, and post-hoc conversion.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The within-model comparisons only partially constrain the training-recipe explanation.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: The within-model pairings on Gemma-2-2B and Gemma-3-1B and the activation-function-controlled comparison partially constrain the recipe factor.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The causal effects are weaker in the 26-layer Gemma-3-1B configuration.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: But Gemma-3-1B at 26 layers shows weaker effects.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Activation-based detection uses a fixed threshold, although the authors report robustness over a 2× range and use an independent detector for causal tests.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Activation-based detection uses a fixed operating point.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The analysis is restricted to the single-token diagnostic endpoint; multi-token spans and compositional features remain future work.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: The single-token endpoint is the diagnostic case. We leave multi-token spans and compositional features to future work, via span-embedding alignment.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The model-scale trend is based on only three points and is descriptive rather than functionally decisive.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: We emphasize that three data points cannot distinguish among functional forms—this fit is primarily descriptive:

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Cross-model prevalence comparisons also vary base model, tokenizer, and training data simultaneously.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: The prevalence gap co-varies with SAE family and cannot be attributed to methodology alone, since base model, tokenizer, and training data vary simultaneously.

threats_not_stated_by_authors: No Gemma 4 E2B model or KV-shared-layer architecture is tested, so direct transfer to layers 15–34 is uncertain.
The intervention endpoint is target-token next-token logit or rank, not induction-head behavior, factual-recall accuracy, or downstream answer correctness.
Residual-stream zero-ablation does not isolate whether effects arise from attention heads, MLPs, value/output pathways, or interactions involving shared KV layers.
Decoder-alignment detection and logit-lens evaluation both use embedding geometry, which may preferentially favor lexical features even though the detector is independent of activation statistics.
Excluding features with fewer than five active positions and sampling a fixed OpenWebText corpus can bias results toward frequent, easily observed tokens and away from rare factual tokens.
The paper does not report whether ablation damages non-target tokens, so the specificity of the observed target-token effect is unclear.
Global BH correction across layer tests may not account for dependence among features, tokens, or neighboring layers.
No runtime, memory, or CPU-feasibility measurements are reported for repeated full-layer forward passes, limiting direct planning of an equivalent CPU study.
data.relevance_to_lab: The paper is methodologically relevant but has little direct model overlap with the lab. Its decoder-alignment detector, residual-stream zero-ablation, logit-lens Δlogit/rank measurements, magnitude-matched controls, and layer-wise anchoring/recovery analysis can be transferred to Gemma 4 E2B layers 15–34 using each layer's token embeddings. Its depth dissociation suggests testing whether features in layers 15–34 directly shape target logits or primarily propagate downstream effects, while its SAE-family results motivate checking SAE checkpoint identity rather than assuming portable causal roles. However, Gemma 4 E2B, shared-KV behavior, induction heads, factual recall, and CPU cost are not evaluated, so a small feature-and-layer subset with behavioral recall tests would be needed before broad activation patching.
